text:
Declan Chisholm is on his fourth NHL team in five years, and he says it's finally clicking. New Jersey Hockey Now ran it under the headline "I'm Coming Into My Own." The numbers back the mood more than the scoring line. With the 26-year-old on the ice at five on five, the Devils have taken 56.6% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, in about 14 minutes a night on a team that has won eight of his last ten games.

Don't get attached to the goals. He has two on ten shots against a chance total that would expect about a quarter of one. That is a 20% shooting rate for a defenseman whose likely range is closer to 7%.

What he does well is quieter. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking (a small sample, five games last season) had 62% of his exits leaving the zone with possession. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level in Washington last year, with chances against piling up in a small sample. In New Jersey, so far, that hasn't followed him.
